claims.title: Complete packet analysis and synthesis
claims.statement_tex:
The maps
\[
 \mathcal A x=(P_ax)_a,\qquad
 \mathcal S(x_a)_a=\sum_ax_a
\]
are inverse isomorphisms between $X$ and $\bigoplus_aX_a$. In particular,
$x=\sum_aP_ax$ uniquely.
claims.hypotheses: Let $P_1,\ldots,P_m\in\operatorname{End}(X)$ satisfy $P_aP_b=\delta_{ab}P_a$ and $\sum_aP_a=I_X$. Set $X_a=P_aX$.
claims.hypotheses_tex: Let $P_1,\ldots,P_m\in\operatorname{End}(X)$ satisfy $P_aP_b=\delta_{ab}P_a$ and $\sum_aP_a=I_X$. Set $X_a=P_aX$.
claims.domain: Vector spaces over a field

claims.title: Transfer algebra and packet paths
claims.statement_tex:
\[
 T=\sum_{a,b}P_bTP_a,\qquad
 (ST)_{ca}=\sum_bS_{cb}T_{ba}.
\]
The block representation is an algebra isomorphism to

intermediate packets. For every integer $k\ge1$, iterating the product gives

 P_{a_k}T^kP_{a_0}

theorem packet_refinement [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S]
    (fine : I → S) (coarsen : S → R) (r : R) (x : I → V) (i : I) :
    packet (coarsen ∘ fine) r x i =
      ∑ s : S, if coarsen s = r then packet fine s x i else 0 := by

theorem projector_refinement [Fintype S] [DecidableEq S] [DecidableEq R]
    (fine : I → S) (coarsen : S → R) (r : R) :
    projector (coarsen ∘ fine) r =
      ∑ s : S, if coarsen s = r then projector fine s else 0 := by

claims.interpretation: The source proves supplied coordinate refinement and its bounded ℓ2 specialization, not every abstract packet operator refinement.

\]

claims.title: Polyphase analysis and convolution kernels
claims.statement_tex:
Interleaving the $N$ channels recovers $x$ exactly. With
\[
 h_{ba}[k]=h[Nk+b-a],
\]
the output channels satisfy
\[
 y_b[q]=\sum_{a=0}^{N-1}\sum_{t\in\mathbb Z}h_{ba}[q-t]x_a[t].
\]
Thus convolution becomes an $N\times N$ transfer-kernel system.
claims.hypotheses: Fix an integer $N\ge1$. Let $h,x\in\ell^1(\mathbb Z)$ and $y=h*x$. Define $x_a[q]=x[Nq+a]$ and $y_b[q]=y[Nq+b]$, for $0\le a,b<N$.
claims.hypotheses_tex: Fix an integer $N\ge1$. Let $h,x\in\ell^1(\mathbb Z)$ and $y=h*x$. Define $x_a[q]=x[Nq+a]$ and $y_b[q]=y[Nq+b]$, for $0\le a,b<N$.
claims.domain: Absolutely summable sequences on $\mathbb Z$

theorem synthesis_analysis (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (x : ℤ → V) :
    synthesis N hN (analysis N x) = x := by

theorem analysis_synthesis (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (c : Fin N → ℤ → V) :

theorem fir_polyphase_transfer (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (h : ℤ →₀ K)
    (x : ℤ → K) (k : Fin N) (n : ℤ) :
    analysis N (fir h x) k n =

claims.title: The arithmetic of residual alias ambiguity
claims.statement_tex:
Exactly $d$ unit-modulus nodes satisfy the same data. Hence the physical node
is unique precisely when $d=1$. If integers $c,b_1,\ldots,b_k$ obey
$Nc+\sum_jr_jb_j=d$, then
\[
 u^c\prod_jw_j^{b_j}=z^d.
\]
For $d=1$ this is an explicit exact de-aliasing formula.
claims.hypotheses: Let $z\in\mathbb C$, $|z|=1$, and suppose $u=z^N$ and $w_j=z^{r_j}$ are known, with $N\ge1$ and integer offsets $r_j$. Let $d=\gcd(N,r_1,\ldots,r_k)$.
claims.hypotheses_tex: Let $z\in\mathbb C$, $|z|=1$, and suppose $u=z^N$ and $w_j=z^{r_j}$ are known, with $N\ge1$ and integer offsets $r_j$. Let $d=\gcd(N,r_1,\ldots,r_k)$.
claims.domain: Unit-modulus exponential nodes
claims.interpretation: Unit-circle power observations, finite alias group, and Bézout/gcd identification.

claims.title: Measurement and decomposition obstructions
claims.statement_tex:

claims.title: No uniform location stability without separation
claims.statement_tex:
Their unordered location sets have permutation-matched bottleneck distance at
least $\pi-\delta$, while their measured derivative moments satisfy
\[
 |m_n-\widetilde m_n|
 =|(1-e^{-in\pi})(1-e^{-in\delta})|
 \le2|n|\delta\qquad(n\in F).
\]
There is no Lipschitz inverse for locations with one constant on all distinct
two-jump configurations, even at this fixed order and with known amplitudes.
claims.hypotheses: Fix a finite set $F\subset\mathbb Z$ of derivative-moment indices. For $0<\delta<\pi/4$, compare locations $(0,\delta)$ and $(\pi,\pi+\delta)$, both with amplitudes $(1,-1)$.
claims.hypotheses_tex: Fix a finite set $F\subset\mathbb Z$ of derivative-moment indices. For $0<\delta<\pi/4$, compare locations $(0,\delta)$ and $(\pi,\pi+\delta)$, both with amplitudes $(1,-1)$.
claims.domain: Two-jump periodic packets of fixed known amplitudes
claims.interpretation: Matched circular location metric and the fixed-order narrow-pulse counterexample.

claims.title: Out-of-band matched identification
claims.statement_tex:
On $X=\mathcal S_K+\operatorname{span}\{m\}$, the functional
\[
 \ell_F(g)=D_F^{-1}\sum_{n\in F}\overline{\widehat m(n)}\widehat g(n)
\]
satisfies $\ell_F(s+am)=a$. The decomposition is direct. If the measured
coefficients have errors $\eta_n$, then
\[
 |\widetilde a-a|\le D_F^{-1/2}\Bigl(\sum_{n\in F}|\eta_n|^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
claims.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal S_K$ be the trigonometric polynomials of degree at most $K$. Let $m\in L^1(\mathbb T)$ and a finite nonempty set $F\subset\{n:|n|>K\}$ satisfy $D_F=\sum_{n\in F}|\widehat m(n)|^2>0$.
claims.hypotheses_tex: Let $\mathcal S_K$ be the trigonometric polynomials of degree at most $K$. Let $m\in L^1(\mathbb T)$ and a finite nonempty set $F\subset\{n:|n|>K\}$ satisfy $D_F=\sum_{n\in F}|\widehat m(n)|^2>0$.
claims.domain: Periodic integrable signals with one known edge shape

claims.title: The scaled interval-edge Gibbs profile
claims.statement_tex:
Uniformly for $z$ in compact real intervals,
\[
 S_Mj(x_M(z))\longrightarrow\frac12+\frac1\pi\operatorname{Si}(z),
 \qquad \operatorname{Si}(z)=\int_0^z\frac{\sin t}{t}\,dt.
\]
The first positive maximum of the limiting profile is $1+G$, where
\[
 G=\frac{\operatorname{Si}(\pi)}\pi-\frac12
   =0.089489872236\ldots.
\]

claims.title: Residualized sparse injectivity
claims.statement_tex:
Every vector $\alpha$ with $\|\alpha\|_0\le s$ is uniquely determined by
$A\alpha$ if and only if
\[
 \ker A\cap\{h:\|h\|_0\le\min(2s,d)\}=\{0\}.
\]
Equivalently every set of at most $\min(2s,d)$ columns is independent.
With the convention $\operatorname{spark}(A)=d+1$ when all $d$ columns are
independent, the equivalent condition is
$\operatorname{spark}(A)>\min(2s,d)$.
For $s=0$ uniqueness is automatic.
claims.hypotheses: Let $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb F^m$ be a subspace, $P$ its orthogonal projector, $R=I-P$, $D\in\mathbb F^{m\times d}$, and $A=RD$. Let $s\ge0$ be an integer.
claims.hypotheses_tex: Let $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathbb F^m$ be a subspace, $P$ its orthogonal projector, $R=I-P$, $D\in\mathbb F^{m\times d}$, and $A=RD$. Let $s\ge0$ be an integer.
claims.domain: Finite real or complex Euclidean spaces
claims.interpretation: Projected sparse null-secant injectivity and the capped spark convention.

claims.title: Sparse noise stability and support thresholding
claims.statement_tex:
Define
\[
 \gamma=\min_{\substack{\|h\|_2=1\\\|h\|_0\le\min(2s,d)}}\|Ah\|_2>0.
\]
Then
\[
 \|\widehat\alpha-\alpha_0\|_2\le2\epsilon/\gamma,
 \qquad\|D(\widehat\alpha-\alpha_0)\|_2
 \le2\|D\|_2\epsilon/\gamma.
\]
If every nonzero true coefficient has magnitude greater than $4\epsilon/\gamma$,
thresholding at $2\epsilon/\gamma$ with a strict greater-than rule recovers
the true support.
claims.hypotheses: Assume $s\ge1$, $d\ge1$, and the injectivity condition of SG-14. Let $y=s_0+D\alpha_0+\eta$, $s_0\in\mathcal S$, $\|\alpha_0\|_0\le s$, and $\|R\eta\|_2\le\epsilon$. Let $\widehat\alpha$ be $s$-sparse with $\|A\widehat\alpha-Ry\|_2\le\epsilon$.

claims.domain: The Euclidean model of SG-14
claims.interpretation: Restricted column separation, nuisance projection contraction, and sparse support bounds.

claims.title: Profiled one-packet discovery and its finite gap
claims.statement_tex:
For an unrestricted scalar amplitude the least-squares profile is
\[
 \widehat a(q)=\frac{\langle Rq,Ry\rangle}{\|Rq\|_2^2},
 \qquad J(q)=\|Ry-\widehat a(q)Rq\|_2^2.
\]
The true mask has $\widehat a(q_*)=a_*$ and $J(q_*)=0$.
It is the unique zero-residual positive-amplitude mask exactly when no other
residualized mask lies on its positive ray. Define the closed rays
$C_q=\{aRq:a\ge0\}$. If
\[
 \Gamma=\inf_{q\ne q_*}\operatorname{dist}(Ry,C_q)>0,
\]
with the convention $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$, then every perturbed residualized datum $Ry+e$ with $\|e\|_2<\Gamma/2$
selects $q_*$ uniquely by nearest-ray distance.
claims.hypotheses: Let $B$ have full column rank, $P$ be the orthogonal projector onto its range, $R=I-P$, and let $\mathcal Q$ be a finite mask library with $Rq\ne0$ for every $q$. Suppose $y=B\theta_*+a_*q_*$, with $a_*>0$ and $q_*\in\mathcal Q$.
claims.hypotheses_tex: Let $B$ have full column rank, $P$ be the orthogonal projector onto its range, $R=I-P$, and let $\mathcal Q$ be a finite mask library with $Rq\ne0$ for every $q$. Suppose $y=B\theta_*+a_*q_*$, with $a_*>0$ and $q_*\in\mathcal Q$.
claims.domain: Finite real dictionaries with positive amplitudes

claims.title: Hankel rank detects the actual order
claims.statement_tex:
Writing $V_h=(z_\ell^i)_{i,\ell}$ and $V_w=(z_\ell^j)_{j,\ell}$,
\[
 H_{h,w}=V_h\operatorname{diag}(c_\ell)V_w^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad\operatorname{rank}H_{h,w}=r.
\]
For $r=0$ the Hankel matrix is zero. The transpose is algebraic and is not
a conjugate transpose.

claims.title: Exact Prony annihilation and location recovery
claims.statement_tex:
The unique monic annihilator
\[
 Q(z)=\prod_{\ell=1}^r(z-z_\ell)=\sum_{k=0}^{r-1}q_kz^k+z^r
\]
is recovered from
\[
 H_{r,r}q=-v,\qquad v=(m_{n_0+r+i})_{i=0}^{r-1}.
\]
Its roots are exactly the nodes. Once the nodes are known, $r$ consecutive
moments determine the coefficients uniquely by a Vandermonde solve.
For unit-modulus nodes the corresponding locations are
$\tau_\ell=-\arg z_\ell\pmod{2\pi}$.
claims.hypotheses: Assume $r\ge1$ and $2r$ consecutive moments $m_{n_0},\ldots,m_{n_0+2r-1}$ are known.

claims.interpretation: Prony annihilator uniqueness, polynomial roots, and matched location recovery.

claims.title: Finite exact unknown-order reconstruction
claims.statement_tex:
Those data uniquely determine the actual active order $r$, every jump
location and amplitude up to permutation, the canonical edge packet $j$,
the smooth coefficients of $s$, and the complete signal $f$ as an $L^1$ class
and as its selected right-continuous representative. The high-frequency
budget is $2L$ complex coefficients. The low budget is $2K+1$ coefficients,

claims.title: An exact residual archive preserves the object
claims.statement_tex:
The synthesis $q+r=f$ is exact. This identity supplies no sparsity, compression,
or recovery-from-fewer-measurements conclusion. In finite pixel space the
full pixel basis likewise spans every image in the ideal unregularized model.
claims.hypotheses: Let an approximation $q$ to an available object $f$ be supplied, and retain the complete residual $r=f-q$.
claims.hypotheses_tex: Let an approximation $q$ to an available object $f$ be supplied, and retain the complete residual $r=f-q$.
claims.domain: Any normed signal space
claims.interpretation: Exact full residual identity and ideal finite pixel spanning; no compression inference.

claims.title: Bounded identities extend from a dense core
claims.statement_tex:
Then $A=B$ on $X$. Consequently a finite packet identity established on a
dense core extends to a completion when both represented operators have
bounded extensions. An infinite projector sum additionally requires a
specified convergent synthesis; bounded finite identities alone do not
supply that convergence.
claims.hypotheses: Let $D$ be a dense linear subspace of $X$, and let $A,B:X\to Y$ be bounded linear operators agreeing on $D$.
claims.hypotheses_tex: Let $D$ be a dense linear subspace of $X$, and let $A,B:X\to Y$ be bounded linear operators agreeing on $D$.
claims.domain: Normed spaces and bounded linear maps

theorem projector_complete [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R] (phase : I → R) :
    (∑ r : R, projector phase r) = ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ (Signal I) := by

claims.interpretation: An explicit dense core and bounded finite projector identity are formal examples; the general bounded-operator extension theorem is not a recovered target.
